Jonathan Larsen adapted another opera by this composer into the musical Rent; that opera shows the lives of four artists in Paris's Latin Quarter. For 10 points, name this composer of Turandot and La boh`eme.

They're not Beethoven, but this composer wrote a fantasia quasi sonata beginning with octaves alternating between A and E-flat to depict the gates of Hell. The note C-sharp is played twice before two C-sharp major chords to begin the second piece of a collection by this composer whose movements are based on the slow lassan (LAASH-un) and fast friska. A repeated high D-sharp represents the title object of a piece by this composer inspired by Niccolò Paganini's second violin concerto. This composer, whose performances inspired a fervor called their namesake "mania," based a set of 19 pieces on the folk music of their native Hungary. For 10 points, name this virtuoso pianist who composed "La Campanella" and the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

The set designer Oliver Smith became famous following his work for a piece by this composer, during which the railroad song "Sis Joe" introduces a group of characters on horseback. In that work by this composer, "Saturday Night Waltz" and "Hoe-Down" include dances between the Champion Roper and the Cowgirl. Martha Graham and Agnes de Mille choreographed ballets for, for 10 points, what composer, who included "Buckaroo Holiday" in Rodeo, and borrowed from the Shaker song "Simple Gifts" in his work for Appalachian Spring?

A Giuseppe Arcimboldo painting titled for one of these people depicts a face composed of poultry with a fish for a mouth. In a novel, the protagonist fires a character with this profession before a hunchbacked girl points him towards Titorelli's studio. In a musical, a character with this profession acts as a ventriloquist during the song "They Both Reached for the Gun." On The Wire, this is the profession of Maurice Levy. For 10 points, name the profession of Billy Flynn from Chicago and Sidney Carton from A Tale of Two Cities.

This instrument's repertoire includes John Stevens's Triumph of the Demon Gods and Alexander Lebedev's Concerto in One Movement. Harvey Phillips was known as the Paganini of this instrument, which plays a solo following a bassoon ostinato at the beginning of Silvestre Revueltas's symphonic poem Sensemaya. Ralph Vaughan Williams composed an F minor concerto for this instrument, which plays the opening melody in Ravel's orchestrated version of Mussorgsky's "Bydlo." In the late 19th century, it replaced the ophicleide in the standard orchestra. The euphonium is pitched one octave higher than this instrument, whose family includes a version of it that wraps around the player, the sousaphone. For 10 points, name this lowest-pitched brass instrument.

Recent performances of this opera have been influenced by the findings of Michael Kaye and Jean-Christophe Keck, who intend their critical edition of it to supersede earlier editions by Choudens and Fritz Oeser. This opera's third act includes a spurious septet and the spurious aria "Scintille, diamant" (sin-TEEL, dee-uh-MAHNT) so it has frequently been flipped with the second act. Near the end of this opera, the protagonist insults his lover by singing a final verse of his song about a click-clacking dwarf. This opera was written so that four villains could be sung by the same bass-baritone and four love interests could be sung by the same soprano, though the demands of the coloratura aria "Les oiseaux dans la charmille" (lays wah-ZOH dahns lah shar-MEEL) often necessitates a separate singer to play Olympia. In this opera, Giulietta's act opens with the duet "O nuit, belle nuit d'amour" (oh NWEET, "bell" NWEET dah-MOOR), an iconic barcarolle. For 10 points, name this opera about a German story writer by Jacques Offenbach.

An album beginning with this word references a rock scene that was first named on Urge Overkill's EP Stull. Guitarist Casey Rice was recruited to play the opening riff of an album with a title beginning with this word, which opens with the lines "I bet you fall in bed too easily / With the beautiful girls who are shyly brave." A debut album whose title begins with this word had its origins in the demo cassettes recorded by its songwriter under the name Girly Sound while an art student at Oberlin; those demos include one for the song "Fuck and Run." A photo booth session at Chicago's Rainbow Club is the origin of the cover photo of an album beginning with this word that shows its artist with an open mouth and her eyes hidden by a purple hood. A 1993 alt-rock album whose title begins with this word contains the songs "Never Said" and "6'1''," and was written as a feminist response to a 1972 double album featuring "Tumbling Dice." Those two albums that each begin with this word are by Liz Phair and The Rolling Stones. For 10 points, what word proceeds "in Guyville" and "on Main St" in the titles of two iconic rock albums?

A choral work by this composer sets Psalm 100 to music in D major and does not include altos. In this composer's final opera in Italian, Deidamia confesses her love for Achilles. This composer reused the interlude from his Israel in Egypt for his The Cuckoo and the Nightingale, a concerto for pipe organ. The final movement of this composer's fifth suite in E major for harpsichord is often called The Harmonious Blacksmith. A vocal work by this composer includes sopranos singing (read slowly) D - down to A - up to B - down to A motif twice. This composer worked as kapellmeister to the Elector of Hanover before spending most of his career in England, where he wrote an oratorio that features the Hallelujah chorus. For 10 points, name this Baroque composer who composed Water Music and Messiah.

Dozens of limestone "reserve heads" have been found in this modern-day country, where an unknown artist sculpted "The Seated Scribe". Ushabti ("oob-shab-tee") figurines were often sculpted out of this country's namesake "faience" ("feye-ons"). Two serpopards are carved on the Narmer Palette, which was found in this country. This country's Amarna style was exemplified by a limestone bust that is missing its left eye. Artists from this country created iconic blue hippopotamus sculptures. Interest in this country's art surged after a 1925 discovery by Howard Carter. Scarabs were a common sculptural motif in, for 10 points, what country where the Bust of Nefertiti was created?

William Henry Prestele made paintings of these objects intended as illustrations for a monograph by Thomas Volney Munson, an early American expert on these objects. A god who is dressed in these objects stands at the foot of Mount Vesuvius in a fresco from the House of the Centenary in Pompeii. A ladder appears to rise from some of these objects carried by two men in Autumn, from Poussin's [poo-SENZ] Four Seasons series, which depicts a scene from the Book of Numbers. Some of these food items rest on a ledge in front of an iron fence in Manet's Gare Saint-Lazare [gar seh-lah-ZAR]. These objects and some leaves adorn the hair of a youthful god in a painting by Caravaggio. According to Pliny, some of these food items were painted as part of a contest which Parrhasius won by painting an extremely realistic curtain. For 10 points, Zeuxis [ZOOK-sis] supposedly painted what fruits in such a realistic manner that birds tried to peck at them?

In one opera by this composer, Mab disguises herself as Catherine in order to be kidnapped in her place. Zurga and Zadir pledge eternal friendship to one another in the famous duet "au fond du temple saint" in a work by this man. Charles-Francois Gounod accused this composer of The Fair Maid of Perth of plagiarism upon the release of a work that begins in a cigarette factory. The title character of that work by this composer sings her "Habañera" before seducing a toreador. For 10 points, name this composer of The Pearl Fishers and Carmen.

He composed a piece in G flat major for baritone, chorus, three yodellers, and four alpine horns called Abendzauber. He chose b flat minor as the key for his Missa solemnis, while he occasionally nicknamed his first symphony "the saucy maid." His namesake rhythm is characterized by a duplet plus triplet, or vice versa, and pervades his sixth symphony. His fourth symphony features a scherzo with outer sections unconventionally in 2/4 time, and he concluded his studies under Otto Kitzler with a work numbered 00, the "Study" Symphony. His unfinished tenth symphony often uses his Te Deum as a finale. For 10 points, name this German composer who dedicated his third symphony to his idol Richard Wagner, and whose fourth symphony is nicknamed Romantic.

Along with objects relating to Christ's passion, rings of figures hold these objects while circling around a glowing Madonna and Child in The Glorification of the Virgin by Geertgen tot Sint Jans. Naked figures hold hands in a ring around one of these objects on a red tent on a cylindrical wooden house in a Last Judgement in Bruges. In another painting, a man standing on one of these objects bends over to balance a large (+) egg on his back. In that painting, a large, pink one of these objects rests on a white disk atop a head glancing sideways. These objects feature in a section of that painting just below the 'Tree Man,' to the left of a bird-like demon eating a sinner, above a section for gamblers. For 10 points, name these objects featured in a section of Hell in The Garden of Earthly Delights.
acceptableAnswers: specific kinds of instruments like lutes

tossups.text: This artist never finished the second figure in a sculpture whose first figure holds the sun in her right hand and rests her left foot on the earth. He began his Truth Unveiled by Time after he was attacked for his failure to properly construct two towers at St. Peter's Basilica, for which he designed the baldacchino and the Chair of St. Peter. This artist sculpted a harp at David's feet, as he leans back to swing his sling, while another of his sculptures depicts one of the title figures turning into a laurel tree. His most famous work depicts four black marble columns and an angel holding a spear pointed towards the titular saint. For 10 points, name this Italian Baroque sculptor of Apollo and Daphne and The Ecstasy of Saint Theresa.

This play ends with one character's marraige to Basileia. One character in this play, a poet, recites such bad poetry that an acolyte is ordered to give him all his clothing in order to get him to go away. Another character wishes to join the city that is the setting of the play in order to take advantage of the law that allows sons to beat their fathers. The protagonist explains to Herakles that he will inherit nothing from Zeus because he's a bastard, shortly after being warned by a parasol-wielding Prometheus that an angry committee of the gods is coming to complain that the titular chorus has been blocking sacrifices from reaching the heavens. For 10 points, this is what play by Aristophanes in which Pisthetairos convinces the Hoopoe to let him found the kingdom of Cloudcukooland?

This man's final symphony was completed by Deryck Cooke. This man depicted a child's vision of heaven in the song "Das himmlische Leben," which he included in his Fourth Symphony. Another symphony by this man includes the text of a Klopstock poem that begins "Rise again, yes, rise again," while another symphony by this man is based on the hymn "Veni Creator Spiritus." This man used text from poems by Friedrich Rückert and Li Po in his Kindertotenlieder and his The Song of the Earth, respectively. For 10 points, name this Austrian composer of the "Resurrection" Symphony and The Symphony of a Thousand.

In his autobiography, the designer of this building said making it was abolition, "in the art and craft of architecture, [of] literature in any symbolic form whatsoever." William Curtiss writes that the central square in this building was an "abode of emptiness" likely inspired by Kakuzo Okakura's Book of Tea. Clerestories and stained glass windows were used to illuminate this building's greenish and yellowish interior, much like the creator's previous Larkin Administration Building. The architect's budget for this 1905 building was only 40,000 dollars, though he was able to install a loggia to separate the "community space" from this structure's other spaces. This building, which was made entirely from reinforced concrete, is five blocks away from the designer's own studio in Oak Park, Illinois. For 10 points, name this Frank Lloyd Wright building made for the Unitarian Universalist church.

In a sculpture by Etienne Maurice Falconet, Milo of Croton struggles with one of these animals while his hand is stuck in a tree trunk. Frédéric Bartholdi sculpted one of these animals in red sandstone to commemorate the Siege of Belfort, and St. Mark's Square in Venice contains a fifteen-foot bronze sculpture of a winged one of these animals atop a granite column. Four bronze sculptures of these animals lie at the base of Nelson's column. Chinese sculptures of these animals include them with either a ball or a cub and are used to guard imperial palaces and tombs from evil spirits. For 10 points, name these feline animals that make up the body of a sphinx.

In one work by this artist, a Native American prepares a gun as he hides behind an outcrop of a mountain, while another of his works is set next to a drinking establishment and shows a nicely dressed man in a top hat try to persuade three other men to vote for him. Another of his political works shows a large line of people waiting to hand a slip of paper to a man in blue. The most famous work by this artist of The Country Election shows a young boy and his French father, who is staring intently at the viewer. A black creature in that work sits at the prow of the boat, and it remains undecided whether that figure is a bear or a cat. For 10 points, name this Mississippian painter of Fur Traders Descending the Missouri.

One structure this architect designed has an exterior with Roman brick and art glass windows and can be found in Oak Park. This architect designed a home in Wisconsin with limestone chimneys and stucco walls which has a western counterpart in Arizona. In addition to the Robie House and Taliesin, a well-known work by this man has a fireplace built of boulders, exhibiting organic design, and is also known as the Kaufman Residence. For 10 points, name this Prairie School architect of Fallingwater.

The 1989 restoration of a painting by this artist prompted the formation of the APIAH, who objected to the removal of a reddish-brown hue from a now-green tabard coat. A large dagger and a statue of a sphinx are concealed by the dress of a woman who reaches toward a white-clad Hercules in this artist's Allegory of Virtue and Vice. A string quartet gathers around an hourglass in a painting by this man that was cut in half by Napoleon's troops and transferred to the Louvre, where it is now the largest painting. The presence of slaves, jesters, and drunken German soldiers in another of this man's paintings drew the attention of the Inquisition, prompting him to change its title from The Last Supper. For 10 points, name this Venetian painter of The Wedding at Cana and The Feast in the House of Levi.

One artist who primarily worked with this material created a series of Meisterstiche entitled Knight, Death and the Devil . Katsushika Hokusai was a master of the ukiyo-e style of works that used this material. By carving an image into a block of this material, Albrecht Durer created a sequence of pieces illustrating the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse. For ten points, name this material, used in namesake "cuts," which is extracted from trees.

A model of this work was exhibited in the west alongside reconstructions of its creator's counter-reliefs and costumes from the Zanguezi show. T.M Shapiro was instrumental in the reconstruction of this building, as carried out by Pontus Hulten. Models of this building are held at the Moderna Museet and at the Centre Pompidou. Nikolai Punin argued that this building was an example of architecture that contained "Modern technical apparatuses promoting agitation and propaganda" and was "a place of the most intense movement." This building, called "the first Russian monument without a beard," was intended to cross a river, and a model for it was carried in a May Day Parade in St. Petersburg. Its interior was intended to hold four Comintern organizations in four glass containers and its exterior was a spiral of steel girders. The last of his symphonies originally premiered as a "symphonic fantasy" and has only a single movement. This painting's title derives from the Dibble House, whose distinctive arched gable window sits in the upper background of this work between its two central figures, who were modeled on the artist's sister and dentist. For 10 points, name this painting of a strict-looking woman and a bald man holding a pitchfork, executed by Grant Wood.

Unison C, twice followed by triplet sixteenth-notes back up to C, opens this symphony's first movement, which quotes its composer's aria "Un bacio di mano." The four-note theme "C, D, F, E" appears in this 1788 symphony's final movement, which closes with a five-voice fugato. The "Great G minor" symphony immediately preceded, for 10 points, what last symphony by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart that was nicknamed for a Roman god?

parts.text: Name this genre. Carl Maria von Weber wrote two pieces, in F minor and E-flat major, for clarinet in this genre. The most famous work for clarinet in this genre was written for Anton Stadler.
That clarinet concerto was written by this "Classical" composer just weeks before he died at the age of 35. The last of his forty-one symphonies is nicknamed "Jupiter."

The tunes of the first movements of several of Mozart's works in A major, including the clarinet concerto, clarinet quintet, and twenty-third piano concerto, begin with these two notes. Please say them in the order in which they come in the piece.

bonuses.leadin: The early 19th century Finnish composer Bernhard Crusell is known for his three works for clarinet in this genre. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Who is this jazz saxophonist who was nicknamed "Bird"?
Parker is associated with this fast form of jazz popularized by himself and Dizzy Gillespie.
This idiosyncratic pianist, composer of "'Round Midnight," is another founder of Bebop. A documentary about him is the fine movie, Straight, No Chaser.

bonuses.leadin: His compositions include "Ornithology" and "Ko-Ko." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This photographer's works include Jewish Giant, taken at Home with His Parents in the Bronx. She also took the photo Child with Toy Hand Grenade in Central Park.
Two children appear in this photograph by Dorothea Lange, which is named for and depicts Florence Thompson.

This 1992 book by Sally Mann was controversial for including several nude shots of her own children. Her son Emmett refused to let one picture appear in the book because it showed him with his socks on his hands.

parts.text: Name this composer of the Russian Easter Festival Overture, whose opera The Tale of Tsar Saltan contains "The Flight of the Bumblebee".
A muted trumpet and trombone play a fanfare in "The Kalendar Prince," the second movement of this Rimsky-Korsakov suite. Other movements include "The Sea and Sinbad's Ship." A
This student and friend of Rimsky-Korsakov wrote the ballet The Seasons, a Slavonian Symphony, the symphonic poem Stenka Razin, and a concerto for alto saxophone.

bonuses.leadin: He re-orchestrated Mussorgsky's A Night on Bald Mountain and featured a solo violin in his orchestral Capriccio Espagnol. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this composer whose Cello Concerto in B minor was premiered in 1895 by Leo Stern.
Inspired by Native American and African-American musical traditions, this Dvořák symphony introduces the main theme of its Largo second movement with a solo for the English horn.

Describe the rhythm of the first three notes of that English horn solo in terms of "LONG" and "short" notes. For example, the words "Let it be" follow a "short, short, LONG" rhythm in the Beatles song.

bonuses.leadin: This composer was inspired by folk music to write pieces such as the Dumky Trio and the American String Quartet. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this French painter who painted First Disc as well as a series of studies of Paris, all of which prominently feature the Eiffel Tower.

Delaunay was considered a leader of the 'salon' branch of this movement in art. Other members of the 'salon' branch were Delaunay's wife Sonia, Jean Metzinger, Henri Le Fauconnier, and Albert Gleizes.

Cubism took its cues from this earlier painter who broke the surface of his paintings into geometric shapes such as in The Basket of Apples. He spent much of his time painting Mont Saint-Victoire in Provence.

bonuses.leadin: This man's painting Political Drama combined concentric, quartered circles of bright color with a front cover of Le Petit Journal depicting the shooting of Le Figaro editor Gaston Calmette. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this artist who also painted innocent-looking girls in Alone in the World and The Knitting Girl. In a mythical scene by this artist, several putti recline atop a porpoise as its central nude figure stands atop a clam shell.
Bouguereau produced most of his works in this style, which focused on values and standards instilled by formal institutes of art.

Academic art bridged neoclassicism with this other broad artistic movement, which emphasized strong emotion and nature. Caspar David Friedrich's Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog exemplifies this movement.

bonuses.leadin: Sheep graze in the background as the title girl looks over her shoulder at the viewer in this artist's The Young Shepherdess. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the Baroque painter of masterful landscapes like The Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba.
This other landscape artist greatly admired Claude Lorrain. He painted Salisbury Cathedral "from the Meadows" and "from the Bishop's Grounds" as well as "The Hay Wain."
Constable made paintings titled for this place in 1802 and in 1828. This place on the Essex-Suffolk border was the location of many of Constables landscapes involving the Stour river.

bonuses.leadin: This artist is the namesake of "black mirrors" that were used to smooth changes in tone in landscape paintings, and he painted works like Coast View with the Abduction of Europa in the 1640s. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this set of violin concerti, which were included by an Italian composer in a larger collection of concerti titled The Contest Between Harmony and Invention.
The Four Seasons was composed by this Italian Baroque composer.
This other family of Italian Baroque composers included Alessandro, who founded Neapolitan opera, and Domenico, who incorporated Spanish and Portuguese tunes into his 555 keyboard sonatas.

bonuses.leadin: One of these pieces uses trills to depict a shivering cold. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this composer of a Te Deum for double chorus and orchestra.

Lully was the court composer for this king. Lully's opera Atys was known as "the king's opera" for seemingly depicting this "sun" king's real-life love triangle with the queen and Madame de Maintenon.

Lully's Atys and Alceste developed this style of French opera. The stiff and dotted rhythms in Atys's overture set the standard for stately sounding music in this operatic style of work, which did not always have sad endings.

bonuses.leadin: This composer and court musician pioneered the French overture, in which two sections are each repeated, with one homophonic section and one fugal section. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this artist known for his use of Ben-Day dots and speech bubbles. He depicted an exploding plane in his work Whaam!
Roy Lichtenstein is a member of this art movement which uses products and images of mass culture. Another member of this movement, Andy Warhol, made many depictions of Campbell's soup cans.
In one work by Lichtenstein, a girl says that "I don't care. I'd rather" perform this action than call Brad for help.

bonuses.leadin: The composition of one work by this artist was taken from a panel drawn by Irv Norick in issue 89 of All-American Men of War. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this painting which depicts three peasant women gathering the leftovers of the wheat harvest.
This realist painter of The Gleaners also painted Women Baking Bread.

In Millet's L'Angelus, a farmer and his can be seen praying next to a small wheelbarrow containing this crop. A family of five is gathered for dinner under a lamp in a Vincent van Gogh painting where it is being consumed.

bonuses.leadin: A small man on a horse to the right of this painting oversees his workers. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this art movement that inspired another artist's depictions of a water garden in Giverny. That artist was able to settle in Giverny due to the success of their depictions of haystacks at different times of day painted in this style.
This French artist painted several depictions of water lilies in their garden at Giverny. This artist's painting of a sunrise lent its name to the Impressionist art movement.
Monet's garden included a footbridge inspired by those in this country, whose ukiyo-e prints inspired many Impressionist artists. Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa depicts this country's Mount Fuji.

bonuses.leadin: The village of Giverny was home to a colony of American artists practicing this style's "Decorative" form. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this 1813 opera that was written at a frantic pace in about 18 days. This opera centres on the Bey's recruitment of the title character Isabella for his harem.

The rapid writing of the 1813 opera The Italian Girl in Algiers was typical of the chaotic work habits of this prolific composer, who eventually burned out and retired from opera for the last 40 years of his life.

Rossini's final non-pastiche opera before his retirement was this work, the iconic overture of which is split into four parts titled "Dawn," "Storm," "Call to the Cows" and "March of the Swiss Soldiers."

bonuses.leadin: The overture to this opera begins with seven bars of pianissimo pizzicato before a tutti fortissimo C major chord reminiscent of Haydn's Surprise Symphony . For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this style of music that usually lacks a standard key and may wander freely through any set of chords.
Schoenberg and other atonalists like Alban Berg worked mostly in this country, where Viennese Waltzes were popularized in the late 19th century.
A father and son with this last name both composed a variety of waltzes including "The Beautiful Blue Danube" and "Tales from the Vienna Woods."

bonuses.leadin: Arthur Schoenberg pioneered this style in works such as Pierrot Lunaire . For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this artist who depicted a woman picking fruit, and a blue idol in the background, in Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
Gauguin depicted "green" and "yellow" versions of this figure, who is held by Mary in Michelangelo's Pieta.
Gauguin spent nine weeks with this artist of Bedroom in Arles before moving to Tahiti. During those nine weeks, this artist of The Potato Eaters cut off his ear.

bonuses.leadin: This artist depicted a young indigenous woman with a white flower over her ear in When Will You Marry?, an emulation of "Primitive" art. For 10 points each-

parts.text: Name this French composer who set poems from Verlaine's La bonne chanson and whose Requiem omits the "Dies Irae" movement.

This suite by Fauré for piano four-hands opens with a "Berceuse" and closes with a Spanish-tinged piece titled "Le pas espagnol." It was written and named for the daughter of Fauré's then mistress, Emma Bardac.

Fauré was a favorite subject of this French philosopher of music. His ponderings about the verbal inexpressibility of music's power was popularized by Carolyn Abbate's translation of his Music and the Ineffable.

bonuses.leadin: This composer's student Charles Koechlin orchestrated the suite from his incidental music to Pelléas et Mélisande. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this violent sport depicted in Stag and Sharkey's which features athletes competing in a ring.
Besides Stag and Sharkey's, this American artist portrayed boxers in his painting Dempsey and Firpo. This man created dozens of scenes of urban life in works like Men of the Docks.
Bellow's Men of the Docks depicts a pier in this American city. Dempsey and Firpo is housed in this city's Whitney Museum of American Art.

bonuses.leadin: Famous practitioners of this sport include Joe Louis and Rocky Marciano. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these figures. Following the death of Alma Mahler's daughter Manon Gropius, Alban Berg dedicated his violin concerto "to the memory of" one of these figures.
Angel of Light is the seventh symphony by Einojuhani Rautavaara, a composer from this home country of Jean Sibelius.

Rautavaara's Angel of Dusk is a concerto for this instrument. Former BSO music director Serge Koussevitzky was a virtuoso of this instrument and wrote an F-sharp minor concerto that popularized it as a solo instrument.

bonuses.leadin: The final movement of a concerto titled for one of these figures "of Dusk" is titled "His Last Appearance" and is part of a "series" that includes a symphony titled for one of these figures "of Light." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this member of the Mighty Five, who also composed the symphonic suite Scheherazade.
The Tale of Tsar Saltan includes this musical interlude, in which the Tsar's son is transformed into the title insect, who flies to the tune of frantic runs of chromatic sixteenth notes.
Rimsky-Korsakov was not the only Russian composer inspired by fairy tales; in this Tchaikovsky ballet, Princess Aurora is cursed by the evil fairy Carabosse to prick her finger on a spindle and die.
